notes: V2-P1-006 (PRD Story S12; roadmap section 6 dataset 3; depends on V2-P1-004/005; depended on by V2-P1-007/008/017). Every number below is from a live probe of the real endpoints on 2026-08-08; none of it is asserted against the network -- the rows are inlined as fixtures. (1) THE TRUNCATION IS REAL AND SILENT. q(adj_factor, ts_code=000001.SZ) returns 6,000 rows beginning 2001-11-14; the same query restricted to 19910101..20011113 returns 2,627 more, beginning 1991-04-03 with adj_factor exactly 1.0, so the true history is 8,627 rows and the cap drops the OLDEST. Adding an explicit full range changes nothing. A whole-market window truncates the same way: 20240624..20240628 returned 6,000 rows covering only 06-27 and 06-28. (2) THE BRIEF FOR THIS TASK SAID THE API GIVES NO TRUNCATION SIGNAL -- 'no error code, no has_more, no total'. TWO OF THE THREE ARE WRONG. data.has_more is present on every response and is True on exactly the truncated ones; data.count exists but reads 0 always, so only 'no total' holds. (3) has_more IS NOT A 'MORE EXISTS' FLAG, it is the server's own len(rows)==limit heuristic, and that was measured decisively: the window 20011114..20260808 holds exactly 6,000 rows with nothing older and still reports True, while 20011115..20260808 returns 5,999 and reports False; limit=2627 on a window with exactly 2,627 rows reports True and limit=2628 reports False. It therefore OVER-reports and never under-reports, which is the fail-closed direction -- and it is why the measured row cap is kept beside it as an independent witness rather than replaced by it. Only the literal boolean False counts as complete; 'False' and '0' are truthy and 0 and '' are falsy, so neither coercion is a fact about the data (the rule _open_flag already applies to is_open). requires_truncation_flag makes an ABSENT has_more a failure too, and is stated per descriptor so that V2-P1-007/008 have to decide it; it is set on adj_factor and on stock_basic, the latter because that endpoint has no measurable cap and the flag is therefore its only witness. (4) THE CAP IS PER ENDPOINT, NOT GLOBAL, and this matters: adj_factor and daily cap at 6,000 (limit=8000 and limit=10000 do not raise it), namechange at 10,000, while trade_cal returned all 13,162 published SSE rows in ONE response with has_more=False -- so a single global constant of 6,000 would refuse a complete calendar. stock_basic returned its whole 5,878-row L,D registry with has_more=False, which places its cap ABOVE 5,878 without establishing where -- and the cap is unmeasurable from outside, because limit=5878 reports has_more=TRUE while limit=100000 reports false, so the flag turns True at whatever effective limit is in force and no probe can push past the real ceiling. '6000 minus 5878 = 122 rows of margin' would be exactly the guess this declines to make; if this endpoint shares namechange's 10,000 the true figure is 4,122. So stock_basic declares no cap and now carries requires_truncation_flag=True, because it was the one descriptor with NEITHER witness -- a response omitting has_more was accepted at any row count with nothing checking it. (5) WHERE THE GUARD MISSES, stated rather than glossed: it judges one response in isolation, so the residue is a server that truncates while reporting has_more=False at a row count under the declared cap. A LOWERED cap is NOT in the residue: raising limit above the measured value (6001/8000/10000) still returns exactly 6,000 rows with has_more=true, which shows the server computes the flag as len(rows)==min(limit, cap), so any truncation at any cap reports True and the flag witness covers a moved cap on its own. A calendar-derived expected ROW COUNT was considered as a third response witness and rejected on measurement: 000001.SZ has factor rows on 64 dates in 1991 that are not in the stored SZSE calendar at all -- trade_cal's SZSE series begins 1991-07-03 while the factor begins 1991-04-03, so those days are beyond the horizon rather than marked closed -- and all 64 are dates the SSE calendar marks open, so that expectation would manufacture false alarms. The calendar is used one layer up instead, where the direction can be chosen: see (12). (6) THE FACTOR IS NOT MONOTONE, contrary to the brief's 'monotone non-decreasing, pin it on real data' -- a test written to that spec would FAIL. Eight of 000001.SZ's own rows step down: five are genuine 1991-93 movements of up to 6.4% (2.608 -> 2.463 on 1991-11-11) and three are four-to-three-decimal rounding worth 0.0002%. Market-wide between 2023-12-29 and 2024-06-28, 28 of the 5,351 securities present on both dates have a LOWER factor on the later one. The contract makes no monotonicity claim and a test pins the eight decreases as data. The five that fell by more than 0.1% are filed SEPARATELY, as delisted_securities_carry_unstable_factors, because they are not market movements: 600069.SH (退银鸽(退), listed 19970430) has 5,421 daily bars ending 20200820 at 0.28 yuan and delist_date 20200827, yet adj_factor serves rows to 20250428 which change 17 times since 2020-01-01, OSCILLATING between two levels (6.415 -> 0.6604 on 20220624, back on 20220906, ..., 6.415 -> 0.6604 on 20240617 -- the step that produced the -89.7%), over four distinct values 0.6603/0.6604/6.4148/6.415. A cumulative factor cannot return to a level it left, so these are upstream defects; 600978.SH (delisted 20210322, last bar 20210222, factor rows to 20250814) has the same shape with 17 changes over 0.8016/5.041/5.0417, and all five (600069, 600978, 600247, 600677, 600485) are delisted SH main-board names. Any adjusted return spanning a delisting is untrustworthy. Filing that under 'the factor really can fall' would have told the reader it was a fact about corporate actions. (7) THE STORAGE DECISION IS PIECEWISE CONSTANT, and the reasons are measured: 8,627 rows taking 43 distinct values, so 42 change points and 44 stored rows (196x, not the 201x that quoting the distinct-value count as the row count gives), against ~4.8e7 rows for the whole market's daily form of a series that moves about once per security per year; the query is a bisect, the same shape NameHistory already uses. THE PARTITION-BOUNDARY HAZARD the brief flags is answered structurally -- load_bearing_observations keeps the window's FIRST observation, every change, AND the window's LAST observation. The last one is the easy one to drop and the one that matters: 000001.SZ's final 2024 change is 2024-10-10, so without it the partition would report covered_through as October and refuse every November and December question. Both anchors are real observations, not interpolated markers. Two adjacent years therefore concatenate with at most one redundant equal-valued row at the boundary and no invented one. (8) TWO HORIZONS, unlike NameHistory's one. A name persists until it is changed, so carrying the last one forward invents nothing; a factor changes on a schedule the held data cannot see (000001.SZ moved four times in the two years after 2024), so carrying the last factor forward asserts that no corporate action happened in a window the read never covered. factor_on refuses both ends and covered_from/covered_through state the window. (9) THE CONVENTION IS BACKWARD, and the brief called it 前复权累积因子, which is wrong: a forward-adjusted factor is 1.0 at the base day and below 1.0 before it, while this series is 1.0 at the listing (19910403) and 139.008 in 2026. 后复权 price = close * factor and needs no base day; 前复权 price = close * factor(day) / factor(base) and adjust_price RAISES without a base_day rather than defaulting to the newest day held, which would silently restate every adjusted price on the next refresh. Passing a base_day to the backward convention also raises, because a caller who supplies one has asked for the other scale. adjusted_return takes no convention at all, and a test proves the two scales give the same return on real prices. (10) INGEST SHAPE. A request is one trading day of the whole market (the same _trade_date_params daily uses): 5,387 rows on 2024-06-28 and 5,553 on 2026-08-07 against the 6,000 cap, so a cross section fits and one security's history does not. A partition is a calendar year = ~1.3e6 rows = ~244 fetches, and PanelStore.write_partition replaces a partition whole with no append, so the fetches have to become one batch first. merge_panel_batches is that primitive (the inverse of split_panel_batch_by_year, and the one V2-P1-007 will need for daily); write_adjustment_factors merges, checks the session census against a TradingCalendar, compresses, refuses a straddling year via panel_partition_year and refuses an overwrite that would drop a security via the shared _refuse_to_drop_stored_subjects. The subject guard and the session guard are the two halves of one failure and neither substitutes for the other: a missing security makes the answer shorter, a missing session makes it WRONG. A merged batch's source_uri becomes None when the inputs disagree, which is a real loss and is stated rather than papered over -- every row still carries its own subject and factor_date, and PartitionCoverage.batch_digest still re-proves the partition. (11) A PRE-EXISTING BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED IN PASSING. _panel_source_uri joined every distinct subject, so a real whole-market fetch built a ~60,000-character URI and ColumnarPanelBatch refused it OUTSIDE fetch_panel's decode try -- meaning no whole-market panel fetch could complete at all, stock_basic's included (reproduced against 2b06c4c with 400 synthetic registry rows). The join is now kept while it fits under the contract's own MAX_SOURCE_URI_LENGTH and replaced by '{n}-subjects' when it does not, so the two-exchange calendar URI is byte-identical to what it was. The producer's bound is BOUND to the contract's constant rather than restated as a second literal, and a test asserts the equality: while they were two separate 2048s, raising the producer's to 3,000 left the whole suite green and restored the original bug for every fetch whose joined URI lands in the gap (9-character codes over a 39-character frame make it 10n+38, so 201 subjects land on exactly 2,048 and 202 land past it). (12) READINESS waives required_dates ON THE RECORD, and this is the one place the storage decision is visible from outside: a compressed step function has rows only on load-bearing sessions, so a calendar-derived expectation would report a permanent date_gap on a partition that is complete by construction -- panel_readiness_requirement must NOT be pointed at this dataset. WHAT REPLACES IT IS A WRITE-TIME CHECK, NOT A PROPERTY OF THE STORED ROWS. The window anchors are not the replacement, and saying they were is the one claim in this row that was measured false: they bound one partition's ENDS, so a hole inside a partition -- or a partition that begins in March -- falls inside covered_from/covered_through the moment two years are read together and is answered by bisect from the previous step, with nothing raising. Reproduced end to end on a real PanelStore: a 2026 partition backfilled from 06-15 reports ready=True with no issues and answers factor_on(2026-06-12) with 134.5794 instead of 139.008, turning that day's return from +2.742251% into -0.530973% -- the unadjusted number, sign and all. Three shapes produce it on real 000001.SZ data: a 2020 partition starting in March beside a complete 2019 (36 wrong sessions, the true step being 2020-01-02), a single dropped cross-section fetch (1 wrong session), and 1996 fetched after that year's last step (50.0000% relative error, 6.984 against 13.968). So compression is preceded by _refuse_missing_factor_sessions, which requires every session the calendar reports open between the year's start and the day before the fetch. MISSING only -- extra days are tolerated, because the 64 1991 dates above are exactly the shape an equality check would wrongly refuse, and an extra observation cannot remove information. Named residues: a year written from a batch fetched on 1 January of that same year is unchecked, and partitions written before the gate existed are not re-examined on read. Beside it, load_adjustment_histories' contiguity rule is STRICTER than load_stock_universe's: a skipped factor year is not a shorter answer but a wrong one, because the last step before the gap would answer every day inside it. (13) THE JOIN. adjustment_factors_on(histories, universe, calendar, day) is fail-closed on both sides: a non-session raises rather than returning a cross section of prices that do not exist, and a security the universe says was listed but the read holds no factor for blocks the WHOLE section rather than being dropped from it -- a partial cross section is indistinguishable from a smaller market. (14) TWO PRE-EXISTING ASSERTIONS WERE UPDATED because this task made them false, both forced rather than weakened: test_tushare_metadata_declares_supported_datasets pinned four dataset names and now pins five (still an exact literal), and test_an_unsupported_dataset_is_refused_by_fetch_panel used 'adj_factor' as its stand-in for an unknown dataset and now uses 'not_a_tushare_endpoint'. (15) MUTATION TESTING: 27 mutants covering every guard added here -- the has_more identity check, the flag-absent branch, the cap's >= boundary, the bool and non-positive factor refusals, the source_uri fallback, both compression anchors, both horizons, the forward/backward base_day rules, adjusted_return's factors, the duplicate-day refusal, the cross-section hole and closed-day refusals, merge's clock and dataset checks, the write path's compression and subject guard, the year-gap rule, and the null-factor and repeated-session refusals in compress_adjustment_batch -- were applied and all 27 killed. A review then applied 34 mutants this task had not, of which 6 survived; every survivor is now closed by a test: the two source_uri length constants are bound together and asserted equal (the 2048 -> 3000 mutant now dies), compress_adjustment_batch's sort is pinned by feeding it Tushare's own DESCENDING order, merge_panel_batches' schema_version refusal joined the parametrisation that already covered provider_id and kind, the KNOWN_ADJUSTMENT_LIMITATIONS test became set EQUALITY instead of three memberships that left two entries outside its own sample, the exact-type float check is pinned with a float SUBCLASS (which is what type(...) is float actually refuses -- isinstance(True, float) is already False, so bool does not distinguish the two spellings; the provider-side type is float or type is int is the check that genuinely turns on bool), and the 2,048-character URI boundary is parametrised at 200/201/202 subjects. Layering unchanged: the contract lives in domain/ (pure datetime, bisect, dataclasses, math.isfinite), openalpha_cn.panel imports no sibling subpackage, lint-imports 4 kept / 0 broken, runtime dependencies unchanged at 9. Backend 962 passed + 1 skipped (was 943 + 1), coverage 93.43% (was 93.39%), frontend 52 passed unchanged.

feature_name: Daily bars and valuations with a two-path return cross-check
feature_description: daily and daily_basic wired onto the descriptor table as V2-P1-007's dataset (4), plus the DailyBar/DailyValuation contracts, the return cross-validation that exercises them against V2-P1-006's adjustment factors, and the cross section that joins a session's bars onto the listed universe. The roadmap routes this issue onto the panel plane because kind='daily' evidence records are refused by evidence/builder.py. Tushare's pre_close is already restated for the morning's corporate action, so a session return has two correct forms (close/pre_close, and the adjusted ratio) and one that is wrong with the sign reversed on every ex-rights day; session_returns computes all three and refuses when the two correct ones disagree by more than one published tick. daily_basic republishes close, which makes the two fetches a session needs into a free cross-check, and write_daily_panel makes that agreement a precondition of storage. total_mv, circ_mv and turnover_rate reach the panel as P3 neutralisation and P4 leaderboard inputs.
acceptance_test: tests/integration/panel/test_daily_panel_ingest.py::test_the_stored_panel_answers_the_ex_dividend_day_on_both_correct_paths
notes: V2-P1-007 (PRD Story S4; roadmap section 6 dataset 4; depends on V2-P1-004/005/006; depended on by V2-P1-008/017, P3 neutralisation, P4 leaderboards). Every number below is from a live probe of the real endpoints on 2026-08-08/09; none of it is asserted against the network -- the rows are inlined as fixtures. (1) FETCH GRANULARITY IS ONE SESSION OF THE MARKET. daily(trade_date=20240628) returns 5,338 rows and daily_basic 5,338, against a measured 6,000-row per-response cap; 20260807 returns 5,535 for both, so the headroom is ~8%. A bare daily(ts_code=000001.SZ) and a bare daily_basic(ts_code=000001.SZ) each return exactly 6,000 rows with has_more=True, so a per-security history cannot be stored at all. Both descriptors therefore reuse _trade_date_params and V2-P1-006's merge_panel_batches, and the year is ~244 fetches per dataset. (2) pre_close IS ALREADY EX-RIGHTS ADJUSTED, which is the whole point. 000001.SZ closed at 11.30 on 2026-06-11 and its 2026-06-12 pre_close is 10.94, not 11.30. So close/pre_close-1 = +2.742230% and (close*f)/(prev_close*f_prev)-1 = +2.742251% agree, while close[t]/close[t-1]-1 = -0.530973% has the wrong sign. On the market-wide 2026-06-11/12 pair, 100 of 5,508 securities had a pre_close more than one fen from the previous close. session_returns() computes all three and REFUSES when the two correct paths disagree by more than one published tick of pre_close (0.01). The tolerance is stated in price space rather than return space because the same half-fen of rounding is 4.6e-4 of relative error on an 11-yuan stock and 3.3e-3 on a 1.50-yuan one. Measured across 16,246 real (previous session, session) pairs on three sessions, the largest disagreement was 0.0081 and the naive path was wrong by up to 118.30. (3) THE 49-NAME GAP IS TWO POPULATIONS, NOT ONE. On 2024-06-28 adj_factor served 5,387 rows and daily 5,338, with daily a strict subset. Of the 49: 26 were listed and halted (all 26 appear in that session's 28-row suspend_d) and 23 had already been delisted (delist_date <= 20240628) and still emit factor rows -- 600069.SH and 600247.SH among them, the names KNOWN_ADJUSTMENT_LIMITATIONS.delisted_securities_carry_unstable_factors already carries. priced_cross_section() keeps them apart without suspend_d (V2-P1-008) because it iterates universe.listed_on(day): the 23 never become candidates and the 26 land in PricedCrossSection.unpriced by name. (4) A PRICED SECURITY CAN BE ABSENT FROM THE REGISTRY. 300114.SZ has a real 2024-06-28 bar and stock_basic returns zero rows for it under 'L', 'D', 'P', 'L,D' and the bare request. It is the only such name on that session and there are none on 20250801 or 20260807. PricedCrossSection.unlisted_bars names these rather than keeping them (a code is_listed refuses to answer for) or dropping them (a market short by one, with no signal). (5) daily_basic IS A SUBSET OF daily, NEVER A SUPERSET, AND THE GAP IS ONE BOARD. 20150708: 1,489 / 1,467. 20180102: 3,282 / 3,252. 20200302: 3,843 / 3,783. 20220425: 4,836 / 4,780. 20240628 and 20260807: zero difference. Every missing code on every one of those sessions ends in .BJ. So close_disagreements() reports a valuation with no bar (never observed, a contradiction) and tolerates a bar with no valuation (ordinary), and write_daily_panel() refuses the first at write time. The close columns agreed on all 24,188 shared rows of five sessions. (6) NULLABILITY IS MEASURED, NOT REASONED. On 20240628, of 5,338 daily_basic rows: pe null on 1,102, pe_ttm 1,214, dv_ttm 1,840, dv_ratio 354, pb 29, ps/ps_ttm 3, volume_ratio 2 -- those eight are DAILY_BASIC_NULLABLE_COLUMNS. close, turnover_rate, turnover_rate_f, total_share, float_share, free_share, total_mv and circ_mv were populated on every row of five sessions across 2023..2026 and a null in one is refused at the provider boundary; a null total_mv would silently drop a name from a neutralisation regression. All 11 daily fields were non-null and all five price columns positive across 24,188 bars. (7) THE TRUNCATION FLAG IS DECLINED, WITH A REASON. requires_truncation_flag governs only an ABSENT has_more; a present one is checked for every dataset. adj_factor demands it because a truncated factor series is silently wrong (the step function answers the missing decade from an older level); a truncated daily response is short, not wrong. The residue is pinned rather than argued away: a response that both omits the flag and comes in under 6,000 rows is accepted. (8) THE SESSION CENSUS IS V2-P1-006's HOMOMORPH AND DIFFERS IN WHAT IT PAYS FOR. adjustment_requirement waives required_dates (compression destroys the census), so its write-time census is the only check and cannot re-examine an older partition. A price partition is uncompressed, so daily_requirement does NOT waive required_dates and every read re-checks the same calendar-derived expectation. Both censuses share _session_census() and both bound the expectation at the year's own start and the day before the fetch. panel_readiness_requirement is deliberately not reused: it clamps at as_of's calendar date, one session too generous for a dataset that publishes at 16:30, and _sessions_published_through reads the same DAILY_AVAILABILITY_TIME the provider dates available_time at. (9) THE ROW-WISE PLANE IS REROUTED, NOT REMOVED. The roadmap notes that kind='daily' records are refused by evidence/builder.py:88-90. That refusal is correct and stays: an EvidenceSnapshot is a normalised citation and a price bar has no _Facts model or EvidenceFamily. daily keeps serves_evidence_plane=True, unlike stock_basic/namechange, because a bar has a single honest available_time; what moves it onto the panel plane is ADR-0002's ~1.35e7 rows per field, and scale is a reason to add an output shape rather than to make the existing one refuse. (10) MUTATION-TESTED. Twenty mutations of these guards were applied one at a time with __pycache__ cleared before each run; all twenty were killed.

feature_name: Trading halts and published price limits
feature_description: suspend_d and stk_limit wired onto the descriptor table as V2-P1-008's dataset (5), plus the halt contract that answers what did not trade and the published-band contract that answers how far what did trade could move. suspend_d is three states rather than a suspension list: an R row is a resumption and an S row carrying a suspend_timing window is an intraday halt, and both mean the security traded, so only an untimed S explains an absent bar. That is the answer to the limitation V2-P1-007 recorded as a_partial_cross_section_is_invisible_without_suspend_d, on the read side through explain_unpriced and at write time through _refuse_unexplained_thin_sessions. stk_limit is the band the exchange published, and AShareExecutionPolicy previously derived one from the board and an is_st flag; the two disagree on 159 of 5,338 names on one ordinary session, so MarketBar gained optional up_limit/down_limit fields that the policy prefers when they are there, with the derived path untouched for every caller that does not supply them.
acceptance_test: tests/integration/panel/test_suspension_and_limit_ingest.py::test_a_stored_halt_corpus_separates_a_halt_from_a_short_fetch
notes: V2-P1-008 (PRD Stories S47/S55; roadmap section 6 dataset 5; depends on V2-P1-004/005/006/007; depended on by V2-P1-012/017 and the P4 leaderboards). Every number below is from a live probe of the real endpoints on 2026-08-09; none of it is asserted against the network -- the rows are inlined as fixtures. (1) suspend_d IS THREE STATES, NOT A SUSPENSION LIST. suspend_d(trade_date=20240628) serves 28 rows: 26 S and 2 R (000615.SZ, 603050.SH), and both R names have a daily bar that session. Every R row on every session probed had a bar (27/27 on 20150709, 5/5 on 20150708, 17/17, 6/6, 5/5, 2/2, 1/1, 1/1). Separately, an S row can carry a suspend_timing window: 20150708 served 1,343 S rows of which 31 carry one, and ALL 31 have a bar while NONE of the other 1,312 do -- the same exact split on 20150709, 20160104, 20180208, 20200302 and 20220425. So halted() is the untimed S set only. That split does NOT hold before 2015 (12 of 18 untimed S names had a bar on 20050104, 15 of 143 on 20080102, 1 of 41 on 20100104, with suspend_timing null throughout), which is carried as KNOWN_SUSPENSION_LIMITATIONS.intraday_halts_are_unmarked_before_2015 rather than assumed away. suspend_type's value domain is exhaustive, not sampled: 537,671 rows spanning 2007-01..2026-12, pulled in windows narrow enough that none was truncated, carry S or R and nothing else. (2) THE 1,529-ROW EXCESS OVER daily IS THREE POPULATIONS AND MOSTLY NOT EQUITY. stk_limit(20240628) serves 6,867 rows against daily's 5,338. The extra 1,529 are 1,418 funds (ETFs and LOFs -- 159*.SZ, 51*.SH, 501*.SH, 16*.SZ, 56*.SH -- all present in fund_basic), 85 B shares (44 900*.SH and 41 200*/201*.SZ, in neither stock_basic nor fund_basic) and the session's 26 halted A shares. adj_factor's 49-name excess on the same session shares only those 26; its other 23 are delisted names stk_limit does not carry. daily is a subset of stk_limit only recently: 60 bars had no band on 20200302, 56 on 20220425, 44 on 20160104, 23 on 20150708, all but 001914.SZ being .BJ codes. stk_limit also has a horizon -- 0 rows on 20050104 and 20060104, 1,408 on 20070104. (3) THE DERIVED BAND IS WRONG ON 159 OF 5,338 NAMES, FOR FOUR INDEPENDENT REASONS. Joining stk_limit onto daily.pre_close for every priced name on 20240628: (a) the Beijing board rounds INWARD -- all 249 .BJ names match floor(pre*1.30) and ceil(pre*0.70) while ROUND_HALF_UP matches only 118 and 143, so 131 differ by one fen (920924.BJ: 7.32*1.30 = 9.516, published 9.51); the same 100%/~50% split holds on 20220425 (87 names), 20250801 (269) and 20260807 (333). (b) ST on ChiNext or STAR keeps the board's 20%: 128 names were ST by the name_history grammar and 104 (all main board) have a 5% band while 25 (24 ChiNext, 1 STAR) have 20%, where _rejection_reason's is_st branch computes a band four times too narrow. (c) A new listing has NO band for five sessions, published as a sentinel up_limit with down_limit=0.01, and the encoding has changed twice -- 100000.0 (SSE 2020, 2022), 1000000.0 (SZSE 2022), 99999.999 (SSE 2024, 2026), 999999.999 (SZSE 2024, 2026). (d) 600182.SH 'S佳通', a share-reform name the ST grammar correctly calls ordinary, carries a 5% band. Nothing about the derived rule is silently changed: MarketBar's two new fields default to None and _price_band falls back to the identical arithmetic. (4) THE SENTINEL IS CLASSIFIED BY RATIO, NOT BY VALUE. A whitelist of the four observed encodings would misread a fifth. LIMIT_FREE_RATIO=2.0 sits between the widest real published band ever measured (1.44x pre_close -- 300740.SZ and 603709.SH on their 20180208 first day, +44%/-36%) and the narrowest sentinel (384x, 688052.SH on 20220425). Both consumers are also correct without the classification: no real bar satisfies high >= 99999.999 or low <= 0.01. (5) THE CAPS ARE MEASURED PER ENDPOINT AND ONE OF THEM IS NEARLY GONE. stk_limit serves at most 7,800 rows per response and suspend_d at most 5,000 (20260701..20260807 returns exactly 7,800 with has_more=True, 20150601..20150831 exactly 5,000, and limit=8000/10000/12000 raise neither). The whole-market stk_limit cross section was 6,867 rows on 20240628, 7,216 on 20250801 and 7,733 on 20260807 -- +349 then +517 -- so it sits 67 rows under its cap against daily's 465 of 6,000. stk_limit also DEMANDS the truncation flag, the first price dataset to do so, because unlike a dropped bar a dropped band is not an absence: the execution policy substitutes its derived rule, which is the wrong number above. suspend_d declines it, because every consumer uses a halt to excuse a missing bar, so a truncated response raises more alarms rather than fewer. (6) THE THIN-SESSION FLOOR IS THREE QUARTERS TIGHTER. V2-P1-007's MIN_SESSION_ROW_SHARE had to sit at 0.5 because 2015-07-09 legitimately served 1,363 bars against that year's median of 2,359 (0.578). A full-year census of 2015 -- 244 sessions, one daily and one suspend_d request each -- shows that counting whole-day halts moves the year's minimum to 2,593 of a median 2,796 (0.927), with the binding session moving from July to January where the shortfall is within-year listing growth rather than a halt. MIN_EXPLAINED_SESSION_SHARE is therefore 0.85 and catches a session that lost a seventh of the market unexplained. Three years were censused in full and 2015 binds: 2008 min explained 0.959 (bars alone 0.914), 2015 0.927 (0.578), 2018 0.984 (0.941). 2018's bar figure reproduces the one MIN_SESSION_ROW_SHARE's docstring already published, which is what makes the other two checkable rather than asserted, and 2008 is in the set precisely because it predates the intraday marker, so it is the year where halted() over-counts most. The guard is OPT-IN -- write_daily_panel's halts parameter defaults to None -- which is a real fail-open and is stated as one: making it mandatory would change the signature for every existing caller, and V2-P1-015's panel build, which fetches all three datasets in one loop, is where the default should be removed. The 0.5 floor still runs unconditionally, so nothing is weaker than before. (7) MUTATION-TESTED. Twenty mutations of these guards were applied one at a time with __pycache__ cleared before each run; all twenty were killed.
